purpose: Record what happens to SCK when the missing evidence channel is restored, and why that result holds the gate.

primary.description: Only what textarena 0.7.4 actually delivers to each actor. No reconstruction.

reconstructed_public_vote_record.description: Labelled sensitivity arm. The runner reconstructs the day-vote record the environment broadcasts and then destroys, preserving submission order so an actor only ever sees votes cast before its own turn. Every view carrying it declares the channel and the audit enforces that.

findings: Restoring the vote channel works as a channel: the share of belief decisions where the belief could not rank any legal target falls from 74.1% to 46.5%, for the Villager role from 100% to 16.4%, and in the day-voting phase from 50.4% to 8.6%. The belief becomes a real inference engine instead of a tie-break.
Per-decision quality barely moves: belief regret 0.541 -> 0.533 and belief_planning 0.492 -> 0.503.
Outcomes collapse anyway: the village faction win rate falls from 0.192 to 0.036 (belief) and from 0.304 to 0.068 (belief_planning), both far below the uniform-random plain baseline of 0.146.
plain and memory are byte-identical across both arms (regret 0.643, village win rate 0.146), which confirms the arm only changes the informed variants and that the shared seed schedule is intact.
interpretation: Action regret is not a valid proxy for playing well in this game. Lower regret coexisted with a three-to-five-fold worse village win rate, so the harness's regret metric must not be read as a quality verdict on its own.

The evidence model is mis-specified for play. `recorded_vote_evidence` only ever EXONERATES the player who was voted for (being voted for by a suspected Mafia lowers that player's Mafia probability). The explicitly informed village therefore systematically avoids whoever is under suspicion, scatters its votes, and never concentrates on a Mafia, while the Mafia seats keep a stable target. More inference produced worse strategy.

This is the source of failure step D asks for, and it is an SCK defect, not only a substrate limitation: the mechanism that was supposed to make agents play better makes them play worse once it has data.

gate_decision.reason: SCK has no reproducible, auditable strategic improvement to offer the narrative system yet. In the primary arm its apparent gain is not attributable to cognition; in the arm where cognition actually engages, play gets materially worse. Reconnecting it now would inject an unvalidated component into StoryBox.
conditions_to_lift: replace or calibrate the evidence model so that it can accuse as well as exonerate, with likelihoods fitted on replay rather than hand-specified
re-run the 500-episode comparison and require the informed variants to beat the uniform-random baseline on village faction win rate, not only on action regret
keep the belief-discrimination diagnostic as a health check and require a materially lower flat fraction than the primary arm before claiming the mechanism engaged
extend to 8 and 10 players before any strength claim
